mechanism_narrative: The recent improvement in RETAIL_REC from -11.7 to -8.4, coupled with PARKS recovery from -30.9 to -10.1, signals broadening outdoor and commercial activity that will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks above its last-28-day mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite PARKS remaining above -15 and RETAIL_REC above -12.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stuck near -31 indicates continued policy or fear-driven suppression of high-frequency movement, which caps footfall at transit-linked retail corridors and keeps RETAIL_REC from rising over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean remains below -25 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT remains below -25 for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp WORKPLACES drop to -21.0 combined with RESIDENTIAL rising to 5.7 indicates a work-from-home shift; office-adjacent retail loses more footfall than residential local retail gains, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 8 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises above 5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES fell more than 8 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL is above 5.

mechanism_narrative: In the reopening regime, GROCERY_PHARM holding positive at +2.7 shows essential and mixed retail trips are normalizing; this consumption resilience spills over into RETAIL_REC, pushing it higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +2.

mechanism_narrative: June monsoon or extreme heat onset can reverse the recent PARKS rebound; if PARKS drops more than 10 points week-on-week, outdoor recreation and impulsive retail trips decline, lowering RETAIL_REC next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops more than 10 points week-on-week from its current -10.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its last-7-day mean while PARKS drops more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL at 5.7 means more time spent in home neighborhoods, which supports local retail and recreation trips; this behavioral stickiness raises RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its last-7-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above 5.

mechanism_narrative: Targeted restrictions on transit and offices, visible as TRANSIT below -30 and WORKPLACES below -20, reduce commuter spending and keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks despite the recent retail improvement.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 and WORKPLACES remains below -20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT stays below -30 and WORKPLACES stays below -20 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive at +2.7, indicating resilient household consumption; this resilience will broaden into discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks above its last-28-day mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above +2.
